## North_Pacific Subtropical Front (STF) and Transition Zone Chlorophyll Front (TZCF)

```{r}
#| include: false
### Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(cmocean)
library(here)
library(nmfspalette)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(tidyr)
library(terra)
library(tidyterra)
library(lubridate)
library(elementalist)  # devtools::install_github("teunbrand/elementalist")
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# Set report year (RptYr), to make things easier
RptYr <- 2025

# Set path to variable: Fisheries Indicators
# This is where the data are and where the plots will go
Dir <- here('Fronts')
# Check if it exists; if not, create it
if (!dir.exists(Dir)) {
  dir.create(Dir)
}
```

```{r}
#| include: false

#----------------------------------------------------------
#   STF  
#----------------------------------------------------------
# Load in first quarter averages for the full time series. 
# These data are downloaded and regridded in pyFerret using the SAFE_clim_data_download.jnl script
# load the chlorophyll data for the figure background
sstRas <- rast(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_SST_Q1ave_', RptYr, '.nc'))
sstRas <- rotate(sstRas)  # this changes it from -180 to 360
# Fix the year indexing and add projection and minmax
yr <- year(as.Date('1901-01-15') + depth(sstRas)*365.25)
names(sstRas) <- yr
crs(sstRas) <- '+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'
setMinMax(sstRas)
# Read in 1 degree data for the front index
sstRas1 <- rast(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_SST_Q1ave1_', RptYr, '.nc'))
names(sstRas1) <- yr
crs(sstRas1) <- '+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'
setMinMax(sstRas1)
# Load the climatology from 1985-2009
tclimRas <- rast(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_SST_Q1_clim_1985_2009.nc'))
tclimRas <- rotate(tclimRas)  # this changes it from -180 to 360
names(tclimRas) <- 'SST_Clim'
crs(tclimRas) <- '+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'
setMinMax(tclimRas)

# Make a 18 degree contour using the 1 degree resolution data and extract the underlying ggplot data
# I'm doing this for calculating the front index (ave of all lats)
p <- ggplot() + geom_spatraster_contour(data=sstRas1, breaks=18)
pp <- ggplot_build(p)$data[[1]]
pp$lyr <- as.numeric(as.character(pp$lyr))
# Make the STF index west of 130°W following Shi et al. 2025
STFindex <- pp %>% 
  filter(x < 230) %>% 
  group_by(lyr) %>% 
  summarise(mean_lat=mean(y, na.rm=T)) %>% 
  mutate(front = 'STF')

# Make a high res version for plotting
pHiRes <- ggplot() + geom_spatraster_contour(data=sstRas, breaks=18)
ppHiRes <- ggplot_build(pHiRes)$data[[1]]
ppHiRes$lyr <- as.numeric(as.character(ppHiRes$lyr))

# Start a loop over all the years and make a plot with background SST for that year, the current year contour, the climatological contour, and all previous year contours as lighter 'ghost' lines
#for (i in seq_along(yr)) { # Use this if you are making all the figures starting in 1985
for (i in which(yr==RptYr)) { # Use this if you are only making a figure for the report year

  # Make subset data for the ith year and the ghost lines separately
  sstNow <- ppHiRes %>% filter(lyr == yr[i])
  sstGhost <- ppHiRes %>% filter(lyr <= yr[i])
  
  psst <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data=sstRas[[i]]) +
    geom_path(data=sstGhost, aes(x, y, group=lyr), color='lightgray', linewidth=0.3) + 
    geom_spatraster_contour(data=tclimRas, breaks=18, color='black', linetype='dashed', linewidth=0.7) +
    geom_path(data=sstNow, aes(x, y, group=lyr), color='black', linewidth=0.5) +
    coord_sf(expand = F, xlim=c(180,240), ylim=c(5,45)) +
    #borders('world2', fill='#A5A5A5', colour='gray40', linewidth=0.2) +
    annotation_borders('world2', fill='#A5A5A5', colour='gray40', linewidth=0.2) +
    annotate('text', x=-Inf, y=Inf, label=yr[i], vjust=2, hjust=-0.5) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(name = "SST", colors = rev(nmfs_palette('waves')(3)), limits = c(3.9, 30)) + #indicator-dependent color and scale from above
    scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(5,45,by=10)) +
xlab("") + ylab("") +
    theme_bw() + 
    theme(panel.grid = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.1),
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = 'transparent'),
          legend.key.height = unit(1, "null"),
          legend.key.width = unit(0.5, 'cm'),
          legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + 
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title.position='right', title="Temperature (°C)",
                                 title.theme=element_text(angle=270, hjust=0.5, vjust=0.5)))
  
  ggsave(filename = paste0(Dir, '/STFfigures/SAFE_STFfigs_', yr[i], '_terra.png'), plot = psst, width=6, height=4, dpi=300, units='in')
}

```

```{r}
#| include: false

#----------------------------------------------------------
#   TCZF
#----------------------------------------------------------
# load the chlorophyll data for the figure background
chlRas <- rast(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_CHL_Q1ave_', RptYr, '.nc'))
chlRas <- rotate(chlRas)  # this changes it from -180 to 360
# Fix the year indexing and add projection and minmax
yr <- year(as.Date('1901-01-15') + depth(chlRas)*365.25)  # the time stamp is saved as depth in this file
names(chlRas) <- yr
crs(chlRas) <- '+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'
setMinMax(chlRas)

# And 1 degree resolution for the contour line and for the front index calculations
chlRas1 <- rast(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_CHL_Q1ave1_', RptYr, '.nc'))
names(chlRas1) <- yr
crs(chlRas1) <- '+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'
setMinMax(chlRas1)

# # 0.5 degree resolution
# chlRas05 <- rast(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_CHL_Q1ave050_', RptYr, '.nc'))
# names(chlRas05) <- yr
# crs(chlRas05) <- '+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'
# setMinMax(chlRas05)

# load the climatology
cclimRas <- rast(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_CHL_Q1_clim_1998_2009_050deg.nc'))
names(cclimRas) <- 'CHL_Clim'
crs(cclimRas) <- '+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'
setMinMax(cclimRas)
# cut the climatology at 26°N to avoid the southern contour line
extN <- ext(cclimRas)
extN$ymin <- 26
cclimRas <- crop(cclimRas, extN)

# Make a 0.2 contour and extract the underlying ggplot data
# I'm doing this because the chl data is messy, and this way I can pick just the longest contour and plot that
# This is also helpful for calculating the front index (ave of all lats)
p <- ggplot() + geom_spatraster_contour(data=chlRas1, breaks=0.2)
pp <- ggplot_build(p)$data[[1]]
pp$lyr <- as.numeric(as.character(pp$lyr))

# Find the longest contour for each year
pieceMax <- pp %>%
  group_by(lyr, piece) %>%
  summarise(length=n()) %>%
  slice_max(length) %>% 
  ungroup()
# join the contour data with the longest piece data to remove all data but for the longest contour
contourDat <- left_join(pieceMax, pp)
# Make the tzcf index (the mean lat for each year) west of 130°W following Shi et al. 2025
TZCFindex <- contourDat %>% 
  filter(x < 230) %>% 
  group_by(lyr) %>% 
  summarise(mean_lat=mean(y, na.rm=T)) %>% 
  mutate(front = 'TZCF')

# Start a loop over all the years and make a plot with background chl for that year, the current year contour, the climatological contour, and all previous year contours as lighter 'ghost' lines
for (i in seq_along(yr)) {
  # Subset by year and rescale the spatraster for better color plotting
  test <- chlRas[[i]]
  test2 <- ifel(test < 1, test*500, test+499)
  # Make subset data for the ith year and the ghost lines separately
  chlNow <- contourDat %>% filter(lyr == yr[i])
  chlGhost <- contourDat %>% filter(lyr <= yr[i])
  
  # make plot
  pchl <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data=test2) +
    geom_path(data=chlGhost, aes(x, y, group=lyr), color='lightgray', linewidth=0.3) + 
    geom_spatraster_contour(data=cclimRas, breaks=0.2, color='black', linetype='dashed', linewidth=0.5) +
    geom_path(data=chlNow, aes(x, y, group=lyr), color='black', linewidth=0.5) +
    annotation_borders('world2', fill='#A5A5A5', colour='gray40', linewidth=0.2) +
    annotate('text', x=-Inf, y=Inf, label=yr[i], vjust=2, hjust=-0.5) +
    coord_sf(expand = F, xlim=c(180,240), ylim=c(5,45)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(5,45,by=10)) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(name = "CHL", colors =
                           c(nmfs_palette('seagrass')(32),'black'),
                         values=scales::rescale(c(seq(0,200,10),
                                                  seq(225,500,25),519)),
                         breaks=c(seq(0,500,50),519), labels= ~ifelse(.x<500, .x/500, .x-499), limits=c(0,519)) + # we have to undo the rescaling that we did in the geom_raster for the labels
    xlab("") + ylab("") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.1),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = 'transparent'),
      legend.key.height = unit(1, "null"),
      legend.key.width = unit(0.5, 'cm'),
      legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    title.position = 'right',
    title = expression(Chlorophyll - a ~ Concentration ~ (mg / m^3)),
    title.theme = element_text(
      angle = 270,
      hjust = 0.5,
      vjust = 0.5
    )
  ))
  
  ggsave(filename = paste0(Dir, '/TZCFfigures/SAFE_TZCFfigs_', yr[i], '_terra.png'), plot = pchl, width=6, height=4, dpi=300, units='in')
  
}

```

```{r}
#| include: false

# Make a plot for both the TZCF and STF index. 
# We defined the index as the mean latitude for the front between 180-120°W (following Shi et al. 2025)
# make a plot
Index <- rbind(TZCFindex, STFindex) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(year = lyr)

# Make linear models and extract slope, intercept, and p-values
# STF
lmSTF <- lm(mean_lat ~ lyr, data = STFindex)
f <- summary(lmSTF)$fstatistic
pSTF <- pf(f[1], f[2], f[3], lower.tail = FALSE)
interceptSTF <- coef(lmSTF)[1]
slopeSTF <- coef(lmSTF)[2]
# TZCF
lmTZCF <- lm(mean_lat ~ lyr, data = TZCFindex)
f <- summary(lmTZCF)$fstatistic
pTZCF <- pf(f[1], f[2], f[3], lower.tail = FALSE)
slopeTZCF <- coef(lmTZCF)[2]
interceptTZCF <- coef(lmTZCF)[1]

# Create color palette for easy reference 
oceans <- nmfs_palette("oceans")(4) # 1 = report_year, 3 = previous years
crustacean <- nmfs_palette("crustacean")(4) # 1 = linear trend
coral <- nmfs_palette("coral")(3) # 3 = annual average for Rpt Yr
ann_grey <- "#A5AAAF" # annual means; in NMFS branding guide as dove gray tint 1
waves <- nmfs_palette("waves")(3) # annual means; in NMFS branding guide but not in package
seagrass <- nmfs_palette("seagrass")(3)

# Defining the theme up front so we don't have to repeat it
plotTheme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color='#F1F3F3'),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color='#F1F3F3'),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        plot.background = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"), 
        axis.text = element_text(size=12),
        legend.position = 'bottom', 
        legend.background = element_rect_round(fill = 'gray90', color='transparent', radius = 0.3),
        legend.text = element_text(size=10), legend.key.spacing.y = unit(-0.13,'cm'), legend.key.spacing.x = unit(0.5,'cm'))

# Make plot
ptrend <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = STFindex, aes(x = lyr, y = mean_lat, color='L1'), linewidth=1) +
  geom_line(data = TZCFindex, aes(x = lyr, y = mean_lat, color='L2'), linewidth=1) +
  geom_smooth(data = STFindex, aes(x = lyr, y = mean_lat, color='L3'), method='lm', se=F) +
  geom_smooth(data = TZCFindex, aes(x = lyr, y = mean_lat, color='L4'), method='lm', se=F) +
  geom_line(data = STFindex %>% filter(lyr>=(RptYr-1)), aes(x = lyr, y = mean_lat, color="L5"), linewidth=1) +
  geom_line(data = TZCFindex %>% filter(lyr>=(RptYr-1)), aes(x = lyr, y = mean_lat, color="L6"), linewidth=1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    'L1' = oceans[4],
    'L2' = waves[3],
    'L3' = oceans[2],
    'L4' = waves[1],
    'L5' = coral[2], 
    'L6' = crustacean[2], name=NULL),
    breaks = c("L1", "L2", "L3", "L4", "L5", "L6"), labels=c(paste0('STF Jan-Mar avg, 1985-',RptYr-1), paste0('TZCF Jan-Mar avg, 1998-',RptYr-1), 'STF long-term trend', 'TZCF long-term trend', paste('STF Jan-Mar avg,',RptYr), paste('TZCF Jan-Mar avg,',RptYr))
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Year",
                     breaks = c(seq(1985,2025,5)),  # major breaks
                     expand = c(0,1)) + # remove padding
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Mean Latitude (°N)",
                     limits = c(min(STFindex$mean_lat)-0.5, max(TZCFindex$mean_lat)+0.5),
                     expand = c(0,0)) + # remove padding
  guides(color=guide_legend(title=NULL)) +
  plotTheme

ggsave(filename = paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_FrontTrend_', RptYr, '.pdf'), plot = ptrend, width=7, height=5, dpi=300, units='in')

```

**Rationale:** The STF is targeted by the swordfish fishery. Additionally, both the STF and TZCF are used as migration and foraging corridors by both commercially valuable and protected species. Northward displacement of the frontal zone can increase the distance fishing vessels must travel to set their gear. This can, in turn, increase operational expenses. The positions of the fronts vary in response to natural climate variations. Long-term northward displacement of the frontal zone may also result from anthropogenic climate change.\
\
**Status:** During the first quarter of `r RptYr`, the STF was north of average across the entirety of the fishing grounds. Though, unlike 2022, it was not near its historical northern limits except east of 140°W. The TZCF was north of average across the entirety of the fishing grounds, and west of 155°W it neared its historical northern limits. The STF and TZCF index both show a significant positive trend with a rate of increase of `r signif(slopeSTF,1)` and `r signif(slopeTZCF,1)` degrees longitude per year respectively. The STF has shifted north by `r signif(STFindex$mean_lat[which(STFindex$lyr == RptYr)]-STFindex$mean_lat[1],3)` degrees since 1985 and the TZCF by `r signif(TZCFindex$mean_lat[which(TZCFindex$lyr == RptYr)]-TZCFindex$mean_lat[1],3)` since 1998. \
\
**Description:** The subtropical front (STF) is marked by the 18 °C sea surface temperature (SST) isotherm and the transition zone chlorophyll front (TZCF) by the 0.2 mg/m^3^ chl-a isopleth (Bograd et al. 2004; Polovina et al. 2001). They roughly mark the northern boundary of the North Pacific subtropical gyre as well as the northern extent of the Hawaiʻi-based longline fishery. Both fronts migrate meridionally on a seasonal basis and their positions are impacted by the phase of the El Niño – Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Due to significant seasonal variation, the climatology, anomaly, and trend (`r RptYr`) are presented for the first quarter of the year only. The STF is determined from CoralTemp data (see SST indicator) and the TZCF is determined from ESA CCI data (see Section 0).The STF and TZCF indexes measure the latitudinal shifts of the fronts between 180° and 130°W, following Shi et al., (2025).\
\
**Timeframe:** Annual, seasonal\
\
**Region:** Hawaiʻi longline region: 5° – 45°N, 180° – 120°W\
\
**Measurement Platform:** Satellite\
\
**Data available at:** https://oceanwatch.pifsc.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/CRW_sst_v3_1_monthly and https://oceanwatch.pifsc.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/esa-cci-chla-monthly-v6-0.html.\
\
**Sourced from:** Bograd et al. (2004), Polovina et al. (2001), Shi et al. (2025), and NOAA OceanWatch (2026a; 2026b).\
\
